subject.title: fix(browser): use public ssrf runtime import in CDP proxy bypass

question: Should the `registerManagedProxyBrowserCdpBypass` helper remain owner-scoped/private, or should it become part of the public `openclaw/plugin-sdk/ssrf-runtime` contract?
rationale: This PR cannot be fixed by changing the import string alone; making it compile requires either a private packaged-resolution repair or a public SDK/security-boundary expansion that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Private Access
options.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin resolver or staging mechanism and keep public `ssrf-runtime` unchanged.

options.title: Approve Public SDK Promotion
options.body: Promote the helper to public `ssrf-runtime` only with explicit SDK/security approval, docs, metadata, guardrails, and package smoke proof.

options.title: Pick A Canonical Replacement
options.body: Pause this import-only PR if maintainers want a sibling PR or new branch to own the broader boundary fix.

recommendation.title: Preserve Owner-Scoped Private Access
recommendation.body: Repair the packaged Browser/Ollama load path through the existing private bundled-plugin resolver or staging mechanism and keep public `ssrf-runtime` unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is an SDK/package-boundary decision, and steipete appears in the relevant private-boundary hardening and merge history.
